To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the robustness of an OSN can be increased by controlling agents with low utility in the core or in the periphery of an OSN.

(1) the core of the OSN consists of a few agents with a high reputation, (2) these agents are crucial for the robustness of OSN, (3) a small fraction of agents in the core can be influenced such that drop out cascade are reduced, (4) the robustness of an OSN can be improved significantly by controlling agents in the core.
the coreness value can be used as a robustness measure for the OSN and that interventions in the OSN are most efficient when they target the core of the OSN.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach for robustness analysis of socio technical systems, and with the design and implementation of network interventions.
the robustness of OSN and how this robustness can be improved by means of network interventions.
the development of strategies to increase the robustness of OSN by means that are feasible in practice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the robustness of OSN can be significantly increased by targeted interventions on agents in the core or periphery.
our approach is promising, but needs to be further developed to become applicable.
we have shown that the coreness measure is useful for identifying the agents to influence in the OSN.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the robustness of an OSN can be improved by influencing agents in the core of the OSN, while interventions in the periphery are less successful.
we propose a method to identify and control the most important agents in a socio technical system in order to improve its robustness.
we have shown that the core of the OSN should be targeted in order to prevent drop out of users.
The main takeaway from our work is that
interventions in the core and in the periphery of OSN are equally effective in improving robustness.
it is possible to control the robustness of an OSN by influencing specific agents.
a small fraction of users can be controlled in order to improve the robustness of a large OSN.
